title: Harbor Docs case study
headline: A docs site that answers in **under a second,** *rebuilt in nine days.*
lede: Harbor is a fictional open-source queue. I rebuilt its docs and marketing site as static pages with search that needs no server, and moved every old URL across.

sections.heading: Static pages, **search in the browser.**

zones.title: Build
zones.label: Build · npm run build
zones.body: Markdown compiles to static HTML, then Pagefind indexes the built pages. One command, nothing to keep running.

zones.title: Edge
zones.label: Cloudflare Pages
zones.body: The host serves the pages, the search index and a redirect map of every old Gatsby URL.

zones.title: Browser
zones.label: Browser
zones.body: Pages arrive as plain HTML. Only the search palette loads JavaScript, and only when it opens.

sections.aria: Markdown builds to static HTML and a Pagefind index, Cloudflare Pages serves them with a redirect map, and the browser loads JavaScript only for the search palette.

cards.title: From a React app to static pages
cards.body: Every page shipped React to show text. Astro renders the same Markdown to plain HTML, so the pages arrive finished.

cards.title: Every old URL lands somewhere
cards.body: The old sitemap became a redirect map, checked by a script on every build so a renamed page can't break a link.

cards.title: Search that needs no server
cards.body: Pagefind indexes the built pages, and the palette loads its index only when a reader presses ⌘K.

sections.heading: Fonts that cost **a second.**
sections.text: Three font families and an unsized hero image held mobile PageSpeed back. Flip the switch to see what changed.

fixes.label: Layout shift
fixes.before_note: The hero image had no size
fixes.after_note: Width and height on every image
